title: Identity Disclosure
description: The homeowner (EE1) shares personal identifying information (PII) with the Home Hub (P1) during the registration process. This includes names, addresses, and potentially other sensitive data required for account creation.

title: Data Minimization Violation
description: The homeowner shares more data than necessary for the specific purpose of registering an account and enrolling cameras/sensors. This includes potentially unnecessary metadata or personal details that could be used for profiling or targeted advertising.

title: Data Processing for Unspecified Purpose
description: The Home Hub (P1) receives the registered data and enrolls cameras/sensors. The processing of this data for the purpose of 'enrolling cameras/sensors' may not be explicitly stated in the data flow description, potentially leading to unauthorized processing or data usage.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: Guest User (EE2) shares their personal identity information (e.g., name, ID number) with the Home Hub (P1) to unlock the door. This act of sharing causes the threat because the Hub now possesses the identity of the guest.

title: Data Processing for Access Control
description: The Home Hub (P1) receives the access code and uses it to unlock the front door. This processing action causes the threat because the Hub now possesses the code and can potentially use it to grant unauthorized access to the guest.

title: Unauthorized Access to Home Hub
description: The Home Hub (P1) shares sensitive motion/door/sensor event data with the Local Event Log (DS1) without verifying the recipient's identity or authorization. This allows an unauthorized party to access the data.

title: Data Exfiltration or Unauthorized Processing
description: The Local Event Log (DS1) receives the motion/door/sensor events and stores or processes them in a way that exposes sensitive information (e.g., timestamps, sensor IDs) to unauthorized parties or for unauthorized purposes.

title: Unauthorized Access to Uploaded Media
description: The Home Hub (P1) shares recorded camera clips with the Cloud Video Storage (DS2) without verifying the identity of the destination or the recipient's authorization to store such media.
assumptions: The system assumes the destination is a trusted, authorized entity.

title: Data Storage for Unidentified Users
description: The Cloud Video Storage (DS2) receives the camera clips and stores them in a way that allows for the identification of the source (Home Hub) without requiring the user to explicitly consent to the storage of their personal media.
assumptions: The system assumes the user is the sole owner of the media and does not require explicit consent for storage.

title: Unauthorized Access to Home Hub Data
description: The Home Hub (P1) shares real-time motion alert data without verifying the mobile app's identity or authorization to receive this specific data type.

title: Data Linking via Metadata
description: The data flow (DF5) transmits motion alert data in a format that allows the mobile app backend to link or identify the source of the alert (e.g., via device ID or user profile) without explicit consent.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The Mobile App Backend (P2) receives the motion alert and processes it in a way that exposes sensitive user location data or personal identifiers to unauthorized third parties.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The mobile app backend (P2) shares motion-detected notification data with the homeowner's phone (EE1) without explicit consent or a clear, opt-in mechanism. This disclosure occurs at the source element where the act of sharing causes the threat.

title: Identity Linking
description: The data flow (DF6) transmits motion-detected notification data to the homeowner's phone. The threat arises at the data flow level where meta-data about the parties being used to link or identify them is present. The app backend's identity and the homeowner's identity are linked via the notification data, creating a potential for re-identification.

title: Data Processing
description: The homeowner's phone (EE1) receives the motion-detected notification data. The threat arises at the destination element where the recipient processes or stores the data in a way that causes the threat. The phone may store the data locally, potentially creating a record of the user's location history.

title: Data Leakage
description: The mobile app backend (P2) shares aggregated device-usage analytics with the cloud analytics vendor (EE3). This act of sharing causes the threat because the data is transmitted over an unencrypted channel or to an untrusted external entity, exposing sensitive user data.

title: Data Linking/Identification
description: The data flow (DF7) itself carries meta-data about the parties involved (e.g., IP addresses, device IDs, user IDs) that can be used to link or identify the mobile app users with the cloud analytics vendor, even if the data is encrypted.

title: Unauthorized Processing
description: The cloud analytics vendor (EE3) receives the data and processes or stores it in a way that causes the threat, potentially using the linked user data for profiling or targeted advertising without explicit consent.

title: Unauthorized Access to Video Clip
description: The source element (DataStore) shares a video clip with the mobile app backend without verifying the identity of the requesting user or the app's authorization to access that specific user's data.
assumptions: The system assumes the mobile app has implicit or explicit authorization to access the video clip stored in DS2.

title: Data Linking and Identification
description: The data flow itself transmits video metadata (e.g., file size, creation date, thumbnail) that can be used to link or identify the specific user who requested the video, even if the content itself is not shared.
assumptions: The system does not encrypt or obfuscate the metadata associated with the video clip.

title: Unauthorized Processing or Storage
description: The destination element (Process) receives the video clip and processes or stores it in a way that causes a privacy threat, such as storing the video in a database that is accessible to unauthorized users or using it for analytics without user consent.
assumptions: The process does not have strict access controls or audit logs in place to prevent unauthorized processing.
